items.question:
A research analyst at a pharmaceutical company frequently switches between a Claude.ai chat and other desktop applications — her literature review tool, her note-taking app, and a statistical software package — when synthesising research findings. She finds it disruptive to keep switching back to the browser tab.

Which surface improvement would address this friction?

options.A: Switch to Research mode so Claude can surface literature findings without her leaving the Claude interface.
options.B: Set up a Projects knowledge base containing all her research papers so she does not need the literature review tool.
options.C: Move to the API with a custom client app that docks alongside her other tools.
options.D: Install the Claude.ai desktop app, which runs as a native application and can be accessed from the system tray without browser-switching.

items.question: A knowledge management lead at a 90,000-person professional services firm is building a shared Claude Project for the M&A advisory practice. She is trying to articulate the two most important benefits of a shared Project over each advisor using ad hoc chats. (Choose TWO.) (Choose TWO)

options.A: Advisors can use higher model tiers within a Project than are available in individual chats.
options.B: The Project's custom instructions ensure all advisors receive consistently formatted, on-brand outputs without each person having to manage prompt hygiene.
options.C: Research mode is automatically enabled inside a Project, giving advisors live web access by default.
options.D: The Project knowledge base makes shared reference documents — deal frameworks, valuation templates, precedent transactions — consistently available to every advisor in every session.
options.E: Projects prevent advisors from accessing Claude outside working hours, reducing compliance risk.

items.question:
A hospital's IT team is deploying Claude access for three staff groups: (1) nurses who need to look up medication interactions during shifts using their phones, (2) a data science team building a patient discharge prediction model that will call Claude as a component, and (3) clinical documentation specialists who type up patient encounter notes daily using desktop computers.

Which mapping of groups to surfaces is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Nurses: mobile app; data science team: Anthropic API; documentation specialists: Claude.ai desktop or web.
options.B: Nurses: desktop app; data science team: Claude Code; documentation specialists: Claude.ai web.
options.C: Nurses: Claude.ai web on mobile browser; data science team: Claude Code; documentation specialists: Anthropic API.
options.D: Nurses: Research mode via mobile app; data science team: Claude.ai web; documentation specialists: Claude Code.

items.question:
A communications manager at a non-profit organisation needs to write an overview of how behavioural economics principles apply to donor engagement — a conceptual piece drawing on established academic literature. He has no specific documents to upload.

Should he use Research mode, and why?

options.A: Yes, because without uploaded documents Research mode is always necessary to provide grounded content.
options.B: No, because behavioural economics principles are well-established knowledge within Claude's training data, and plain chat is sufficient for a conceptual synthesis piece.
options.C: Yes, because Research mode will find peer-reviewed papers he can cite directly in the overview.
options.D: No, because Research mode only works when the user has uploaded documents to cross-reference against web sources.

items.question:
An actuary at a reinsurance company uses a proprietary pricing framework — a 40-page technical document — as the basis for all her model review work. She wants Claude to apply this framework every time she submits model outputs for review. The framework changes at most once a year.

Where should this document live to best support her workflow?

options.A: Uploaded as a file attachment at the start of each new review session.
options.B: Pasted as plain text into the system prompt field of an API call for maximum control.
options.C: Stored as Project knowledge in a dedicated Project, making it automatically available for all her review sessions.
options.D: Linked to a connector integration so Claude fetches the latest version from the document management system automatically.

items.question:
A logistics company wants to automatically generate a customs declaration summary every time a new freight manifest is added to their shipment tracking system. The summary should be written to a database table for review by the customs team. No human should need to initiate the process for each shipment.

Which Claude surface makes this automation possible?

options.A: A shared Claude.ai Project that the customs team uses to manually process each manifest as it arrives.
options.B: Research mode, which can automatically monitor the shipment tracking system for new manifests.
options.C: Claude Code, configured to watch the tracking system directory and trigger a summary for each new file.
options.D: The Anthropic API, integrated into the tracking system's event pipeline to invoke Claude automatically on each new manifest.

items.question: A CTO at a 5,000-employee energy company is defining Claude access patterns for three distinct use cases: (1) generating code documentation comments as part of the CI/CD pipeline, (2) customer service agents answering energy bill queries live, and (3) analysts producing ad hoc regulatory impact assessments. (Choose THREE surfaces or features that map respectively to these three use cases.) (Choose THREE)

options.A: Anthropic API for the CI/CD pipeline code documentation.
options.B: Claude Code for the CI/CD pipeline code documentation.
options.C: Claude.ai web with Projects for the customer service agents answering live bill queries.
options.D: Anthropic API for the customer service agents, embedded in the live chat platform.
options.E: Claude.ai web or desktop with Research mode available for analysts producing regulatory impact assessments.

items.question:
A recent graduate starting a freelance copywriting business is evaluating whether to stay on the free tier of Claude.ai or upgrade to a paid plan. She uses Claude once or twice a week for short drafting tasks that rarely hit usage limits.

Which assessment is MOST accurate?

options.A: The free tier is adequate for her current usage pattern; upgrading makes sense when usage limits start interrupting her work.
options.B: She should upgrade immediately because paid plans provide access to more powerful models not available on the free tier.
options.C: She should switch to the API because it does not have per-session usage limits.
options.D: She should upgrade to enable Projects, which are not available on the free tier.

items.question:
A research librarian at a university needs to use Claude to extract key themes from a collection of academic papers. The papers are in PDF format, and she also has a set of hand-drawn concept maps she has scanned as JPEG images. She wants to know if Claude can process both types.

Which statement about Claude's file upload capability is MOST accurate?

options.A: Claude can process PDFs but not images; scanned concept maps must be converted to text before upload.
options.B: Claude can process both PDFs and image files such as JPEGs, allowing analysis of both the text papers and the visual concept maps.
options.C: Claude can process both file types, but images must be uploaded as part of a Project knowledge base, not in a standard chat.
options.D: Claude can process images natively but requires PDFs to be converted to plain text before it can extract themes from them.

items.question:
A product manager at a media company asks Claude to build a simple interactive HTML prototype for a new content recommendation feature — a clickable mockup she can share with stakeholders for feedback before engineering begins.

What is the MOST important reason to use an Artifact for this output rather than inline chat?

options.A: Artifacts allow Claude to generate longer HTML files than the inline output character limit permits.
options.B: Artifacts persist permanently across sessions, so stakeholders can return to the prototype at any time.
options.C: Artifacts render interactive HTML output in a side panel, allowing the product manager to preview and interact with the prototype directly within Claude.
options.D: Artifacts enable Research mode to validate the prototype against current UI design standards from the web.

items.question:
An insurance claims adjuster handles two types of Claude work: (1) quick field lookups of coverage terms while visiting claimants at their homes, and (2) detailed written analysis of multi-document claim files at his desk in the claims centre.

Which surface combination best supports both workflows?

options.A: Mobile app only, since most work happens in the field and it handles both quick lookups and complex file analysis.
options.B: API access only, which provides the same interface across both mobile and desktop contexts.
options.C: Desktop app or web for the desk-based complex analysis; mobile app for the field lookup work.
options.D: Claude Code for the desk-based analysis; mobile app for field lookups.

items.question: A digital transformation lead at a retail bank is reviewing AI workflows that currently use Claude.ai interactively. She is evaluating which workflows have genuinely outgrown the chat interface and should be moved to the API. (Choose TWO workflows that represent the clearest case for API migration.) (Choose TWO)

options.A: A senior analyst who spends 30 minutes each morning asking Claude to summarise overnight regulatory news from uploaded PDFs.
options.B: An automated fraud alert workflow where Claude classifies each transaction flag within seconds of the alert being generated by the fraud detection system.
options.C: A compliance team that reviews a dozen regulatory filings per month using a shared Claude Project with standard review templates.
options.D: A loan origination process in which Claude must assess 500 credit applications daily, with each assessment triggered automatically when a completed application arrives in the system.
options.E: A marketing team that uses Claude weekly to brainstorm campaign concepts with three participants in a shared session.

items.question: An HR director is rolling out Claude access across her 3,000-person organisation. She is preparing guidance on which tool is appropriate for software engineers specifically. Which Claude surface should she direct engineers who want an AI agent that reads their codebase, writes code, and runs terminal commands?

options.A: Claude Code, which provides an agentic development environment that works directly with code files and terminal commands.
options.B: The Anthropic API with a custom IDE plugin the engineering team builds internally.
options.C: The Claude.ai web interface, where engineers can paste code and receive feedback without additional setup.
options.D: A Project with all the codebase documentation added as knowledge, so Claude always has system context.

items.question:
A policy consultant is asked to evaluate whether a proposed carbon credit scheme aligns with international frameworks. The evaluation requires referencing both stable principles of carbon accounting (which have not changed in years) and the most recent updates from the UN climate secretariat (from the past three months).

How should she configure her Claude session to handle both requirements MOST efficiently?

options.A: Use Research mode throughout the entire session to ensure all content is grounded in the latest available information.
options.B: Use plain chat for the stable carbon accounting principles section, then activate Research mode specifically for the recent UN secretariat updates.
options.C: Create a Project with carbon accounting documents as knowledge and use Research mode for everything else.
options.D: Upload archived UN reports to provide stable content, and rely on Research mode only for real-time questions.

items.question:
A training developer at a retail company asks Claude to generate a formatted course outline for a new onboarding programme. The outline should include section headers, learning objectives, and estimated durations — structured content that the developer will use as a working template, refining it over multiple exchanges in the same session.

Which output format best supports iterative refinement within the session?

options.A: Inline chat output, so the developer can see each version in the chat thread and compare them side-by-side.
options.B: A Project document stored as knowledge, so the course outline is preserved between sessions.
options.C: An Artifact containing the course outline, which Claude can update directly in the side panel as the developer requests changes.
options.D: Research mode output, so the outline reflects current best practices in learning design sourced from the web.

items.question:
A junior equity research analyst at a large investment bank types the following into Claude:

`Summarize the earnings call.`

The response is a generic one-paragraph placeholder. The analyst's manager says it is unusable for the morning client briefing.

What is the PRIMARY reason the prompt produced poor results?

options.A: The prompt omits context: which company, which quarter, and what audience the summary is for are all absent.
options.B: Claude cannot summarize earnings calls without a live connection to a financial data service.
options.C: The prompt is too short; professional requests require at least three sentences for Claude to interpret them.
options.D: The analyst should have selected a higher-tier model, which requires less prompting guidance for financial tasks.

items.question:
A clinical operations coordinator at a 400-bed regional hospital uses Claude to draft patient handoff communication templates. The output uses casual language and omits standard categories such as active problems, pending results, and escalation triggers.

Which addition to the prompt would MOST directly fix the register and structure simultaneously?

options.A: Adding a word-count constraint of 200 words per handoff template.
options.B: Opening the prompt with: 'You are an experienced clinical documentation specialist familiar with SBAR and I-PASS handoff frameworks.'
options.C: Appending 'Please use formal language' at the end of the existing prompt.
options.D: Uploading a sample blank template so Claude can mirror the visual layout.

items.question:
An internal communications manager at a mid-market retail chain needs two versions of a benefits-change announcement: one for 1,200 store associates (many part-time, English as a second language) and one for the 15-person executive team. She uses identical prompts for both and gets identical outputs — formal, measured, and impersonal.

What prompt element is she failing to vary between the two use cases?

options.A: A constraint specifying the maximum number of bullet points in each version.
options.B: A reference document containing the full benefits policy text.
options.C: A clear description of each target audience, their reading level, and the desired emotional register.
options.D: A role prompt instructing Claude to act as a certified HR professional for each draft.

items.question:
A production planning manager at a 9,000-employee automotive manufacturer asks Claude to compare three supplier quotes across price, lead time, quality rating, and payment terms. Claude returns four paragraphs of flowing prose. The manager needs to paste the output into a weekly operations report that uses consistent tabular layouts.

What single prompt addition would MOST directly resolve the formatting mismatch?

options.A: Specifying the role: 'You are a procurement analyst experienced with industrial supplier bids.'
options.B: Adding the three quote documents as reference material in the prompt.
options.C: Asking Claude to include sub-criteria and commentary under each of the four evaluation dimensions.
options.D: Explicitly requesting a table with suppliers as columns and evaluation criteria as rows.

items.question:
A grant writer at a small non-profit focused on urban food security drafts a federal grant application. She asks Claude to write the organizational capacity section, but the output describes generic non-profit infrastructure — no mention of the organization's 14-year track record, 23 community partnerships, or three prior federal grants received.

What is the PRIMARY cause of the omission?

options.A: The prompt did not supply organizational facts that Claude has no way to infer from its training data.
options.B: Claude avoids making specific claims about organizations without verifying them against a public source.
options.C: The grant writer should have used a Project with the organization's documents stored as knowledge.
options.D: Federal grant conventions require the writer to fill in specific organizational details manually after Claude drafts the structure.

items.question:
A management consultant at a boutique professional services firm sends this prompt:

`Make this executive summary better.`

Claude returns a marginally edited version that tightens a few sentences but does not restructure the narrative, shorten it, or sharpen the recommendations — all things the consultant needed.

Which rewrite MOST likely produces substantive improvement?

options.A: 'Edit this document for grammar and style.'
options.B: 'Rewrite this executive summary to be under 250 words, lead with the single most important recommendation, and cut all background that already appeared in the main body.'
options.C: 'You are a senior management consultant. Review this executive summary.'
options.D: 'Make this executive summary significantly better. It needs major improvement.'

items.question:
An associate attorney at a mid-size law firm uses Claude to draft a memo analyzing three contract clauses. The output runs to 1,800 words. The supervising partner requires all internal memos to fit on one page — roughly 500 words. The attorney submits the memo as-is because she never specified a length limit.

Which prompt element would have prevented this problem?

options.A: A role instruction telling Claude to write as a senior partner who values conciseness.
options.B: A reference to the firm's memo template, which the partner would recognize as a one-page format.
options.C: An explicit constraint stating the output must not exceed 500 words.
options.D: A format instruction to use headings and bullet points to compress the analysis.

items.question:
An actuarial analyst at a regional insurance carrier asks Claude to explain the reinsurance triggers in the company's specific excess-of-loss treaty for an upcoming renewal discussion. Claude returns a technically accurate general explanation of excess-of-loss structures but says nothing about the treaty's actual attachment points, limits, or exclusions.

What is the MOST effective corrective action?

options.A: Reframe the prompt to ask Claude to 'act as a reinsurance expert with 20 years of experience' and retry.
options.B: Ask Claude to search for the company's treaty terms using its web browsing capability.
options.C: Follow up with a second message asking Claude to 'be more specific about this treaty.'
options.D: Paste the relevant treaty clauses directly into the prompt so Claude has the actual terms to reference.

items.question:
An academic program coordinator at a research university is drafting a new course description for a graduate seminar on AI Ethics. She has not yet decided whether the seminar is for computer science students, philosophy students, or a mixed cohort — a choice that would substantially change the technical depth. She submits the prompt without specifying audience.

What is the MOST efficient approach to handle this known ambiguity?

options.A: Request all three versions in one prompt: 'Draft three course descriptions — one for CS students, one for philosophy students, one for a mixed cohort.'
options.B: Submit the prompt as-is and plan to revise the output once the audience decision is made.
options.C: Include 'If anything is unclear, ask one clarifying question before drafting' in the prompt.
options.D: Specify a default mid-level technical audience as a safe placeholder and move on.

items.question:
A regulatory affairs manager at a global pharmaceutical company asks Claude to 'improve' a 400-word section of a Module 2 clinical summary for an EMA submission. Claude returns a polished version that is better written stylistically but fails internal review: wrong register (active voice instead of passive scientific) and still over the section's 350-word limit.

What should the manager have included in the original prompt?

options.A: A request for Claude to explain its editing decisions so the manager could provide iterative feedback.
options.B: Explicit success criteria: a 350-word ceiling, passive-voice scientific register, and compliance with EMA Module 2 conventions.
options.C: The full 400-word section with track-changes showing the manager's initial edits.
options.D: A role prompt specifying that Claude is a regulatory writing expert familiar with EU submission requirements.

items.question:
A logistics operations analyst at a 3PL provider submits this prompt:

`Write a summary of our warehouse throughput performance for last quarter.`

Claude responds that it cannot access external systems and produces a generic throughput summary template. The analyst's manager identifies two distinct missing building blocks that explain the failure.

Which TWO building blocks are absent? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Context/data: the actual throughput figures, targets, and benchmarks were not supplied.
options.B: Role: no professional persona was assigned to guide the writing register.
options.C: Task clarity: 'summary' is ambiguous without specifying the purpose — client report, ops review, or executive briefing.
options.D: Format: no output structure was specified (table, prose, slide bullets, etc.).
options.E: Constraints: no word count or scope limit was provided.

items.question:
A revenue manager at an international hotel chain wants Claude to review a proposed room-rate strategy memo and flag pricing logic that deviates from yield management best practices. The response identifies stylistic issues and some factual errors but does not engage with yield management principles at all.

Which prompt addition would MOST directly fix the missing analytical lens?

options.A: Asking Claude to respond in the format of a structured risk register rather than a memo review.
options.B: Adding a word-count constraint to force a more focused critique.
options.C: Opening the prompt with: 'You are a hotel revenue management expert with deep knowledge of yield management, dynamic pricing, and demand forecasting.'
options.D: Uploading the hotel chain's current rate parity policy document.

items.question:
An environmental compliance officer at a regional utility company drafts a regulator response about the company's 'ERCOT-aligned dispatch protocol' and 'Tier 2 emission credit banking program.' Claude's response is technically correct on general emission credit banking but mischaracterizes the dispatch protocol and uses none of the company-specific terminology.

What is the MOST likely cause of the mischaracterization?

options.A: Claude lacks up-to-date knowledge of ERCOT's most recent rule changes, which affect the dispatch protocol.
options.B: The company's internal program definitions were not provided in the prompt, so Claude interpreted those terms from general knowledge.
options.C: Claude cannot draft regulatory correspondence without a specific compliance role prompt.
options.D: The prompt should have specified a word count to prevent Claude from generating speculative content.

items.question:
A customer success manager at a telecoms company builds two Claude-assisted templates: one for a renewal negotiation email to a Fortune 500 CFO, and one for a churn-prevention chat to a small-business owner about to cancel. She uses identical prompt structures for both and finds the outputs are nearly identical — formal, measured, and impersonal.

What prompt element is she failing to vary?

options.A: The target audience description and the desired emotional register for each communication context.
options.B: The reference material — she should include the client's contract terms in each prompt.
options.C: The success criteria — she has not defined what a successful renewal email vs. churn-prevention chat looks like.
options.D: The model tier — B2B executive communications warrant a higher-capability model than SMB messages.

items.question:
A content editor at a digital media company needs Claude to draft LinkedIn posts for three thought-leadership articles. LinkedIn limits posts to 3,000 characters, but the company's engagement data shows posts under 1,200 characters perform significantly better. Claude's first three drafts average 2,400 characters each.

Which single addition to the original prompt would MOST reliably produce better-performing posts?

options.A: Role: 'You are a LinkedIn content strategist who optimizes for engagement and brevity.'
options.B: Audience: 'This post is for senior decision-makers in financial services.'
options.C: Constraint: 'Each post must not exceed 1,200 characters including spaces.'
options.D: Format: 'Use a hook sentence, three supporting points, and a call to action.'

items.question:
A senior policy analyst at a federal regulatory agency submits this prompt:

`Write something about our new proposed rule on data portability.`

The output is a general essay on data portability principles that does not reflect the agency's rule language and is formatted as academic prose rather than the numbered-section format required for internal policy briefings.

A colleague identifies exactly TWO missing building blocks that explain the two failure modes. Which are they? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Role: no expert policy analyst persona was specified.
options.B: Context/reference material: the proposed rule text was not included, so Claude could not reference specific provisions.
options.C: Task: 'write something about' is ambiguous about what the output should accomplish.
options.D: Format: no output structure was specified, so Claude defaulted to academic prose rather than numbered-section briefing.
options.E: Constraints: no word limit was given to prevent an overly long output.

items.question:
The clinical lead at a 12-person digital health startup needs to draft patient intake screening questions for a remote depression monitoring smartphone app. Her first prompt was: `Write screening questions for depression.` The output restates standard publicly available PHQ-9 items and adds no value for the at-home monitoring context.

Which rewrite MOST effectively adds the specificity required?

options.A: 'Write improved depression screening questions for a digital health app. Make them evidence-based.'
options.B: 'You are a clinical psychologist. Write depression screening questions for smartphone users.'
options.C: 'Write depression screening questions. Do not reproduce the PHQ-9 directly.'
options.D: 'Write 8 depression screening questions for a smartphone app for adults aged 25–45 already diagnosed with depression, tracking symptom changes between telehealth visits, using a 5-point frequency scale, and avoiding clinical jargon.'

items.question:
A portfolio analyst at a mid-size asset management firm asks Claude to identify material risks in a fund's Q3 holdings report before the quarterly investor call. Claude returns a list of generic risks common to multi-asset funds — concentration risk, liquidity risk, currency risk — without any reference to the fund's actual holdings, weightings, or sector exposures.

What is the PRIMARY reason Claude could not identify fund-specific risks?

options.A: The fund's Q3 holdings report was not included in the prompt, so Claude had no specific data to analyze.
options.B: Claude is unable to perform financial risk analysis without a financial data API connection.
options.C: The analyst should have specified a role prompt identifying Claude as a portfolio risk analyst.
options.D: A higher-tier model is required for financial analysis tasks that involve identifying material risks.

items.question:
The general counsel at a 90,000-employee global retailer uses a Claude Project with the instruction: 'You are a senior employment attorney licensed in all 50 US states. Provide definitive legal advice on any HR question.' An HR business partner asks Claude through this Project whether a proposed non-compete clause is enforceable in California. Claude provides a detailed analysis but hedges heavily and advises consulting outside counsel.

What is the MOST accurate explanation of Claude's behavior?

options.A: The Project instruction was too long and the model could not parse the role correctly.
options.B: Role prompts establish a professional lens and vocabulary but do not override Claude's caution on high-stakes legal determinations that require actual licensed legal advice.
options.C: Claude lacks knowledge of California employment law and is hedging to cover that gap.
options.D: The HR business partner is not the intended user of the Project; the general counsel should have asked directly.

items.question:
A medical science liaison at a large pharma company drafts a Claude prompt to create a disease overview for a new therapeutic area. She needs two outputs: a two-page scientific brief for KOL physicians at a medical congress, and a one-page plain-language summary for patient advocacy group members. She uses one prompt for both and adds only the format difference (two pages vs. one page).

Which element, if added separately to each prompt, would MOST improve output quality for both audiences?

options.A: A role instruction — 'You are a medical science liaison' — added to both prompts.
options.B: The clinical study abstracts added as reference material in both prompts.
options.C: Explicit audience descriptions: for the KOL brief, 'audience: specialist physicians with deep disease-area expertise'; for the patient summary, 'audience: patients and caregivers with no clinical training.'
options.D: A word-count constraint aligned to the page-length difference in both prompts.

items.question:
A content manager at a fast-growing e-commerce startup sends this prompt:

`Write product descriptions for these 5 items.`

The output is generic, inconsistent in voice across the five descriptions, and formatted as plain paragraphs rather than the brand's required bullet-point feature list followed by a two-sentence paragraph. The manager's team identifies two distinct building blocks as the primary causes.

Which TWO building blocks are most directly responsible? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Format: the required structure (feature bullets + two-sentence paragraph) was not specified.
options.B: Constraints: no word-count limit was given, leading to inconsistent description length.
options.C: Context/brand voice: the brand's tone, target customer, and voice guidelines were not provided.
options.D: Role: no e-commerce copywriting persona was assigned.
options.E: Task: 'write product descriptions' is ambiguous about what dimension of the product to emphasize.

items.question:
A claims adjuster supervisor at a large P&C insurer is building a Claude-assisted workflow to review claim notes and flag potential subrogation opportunities. The workflow will process 200 claims per day. She is deciding whether to include (a) the company's 15-page subrogation identification manual as in-prompt reference material, or (b) a concise 300-word context paragraph describing the three key indicators the manual emphasizes.

For a high-volume automated workflow, which approach is generally PREFERABLE and why?

options.A: The 300-word context paragraph, because supplying the essential decision criteria directly in the prompt is more efficient at scale than repeating a 15-page document in every call.
options.B: The 15-page manual, because complete reference material always produces more accurate output than a summary.
options.C: Neither — the workflow should use a Project that stores the manual permanently, eliminating per-call cost entirely.
options.D: The 15-page manual, because subrogation decisions are high-stakes and require full policy context every time.

items.question:
A quality assurance engineer at an automotive manufacturer needs Claude to evaluate whether a supplier's process audit report meets the company's ISO 9001 corrective action requirements. She sends the report and asks Claude to 'check if this is OK.' Claude responds with a general positive assessment.

Which prompt revision would MOST likely produce a rigorous, actionable evaluation?

options.A: Add 'You are an ISO 9001 quality systems expert' as a role instruction before the task.
options.B: Replace 'check if this is OK' with: 'Evaluate this report against the five corrective action elements required by ISO 9001 Section 10.2. Flag any element that is missing, incomplete, or non-compliant. Return a pass/fail verdict for each element.'
options.C: Upload the full ISO 9001 standard as reference material alongside the audit report.
options.D: Ask Claude to score the report on a 1–10 scale and explain the score.

items.question:
A program evaluation manager at an international development non-profit is building a prompt template for impact report summaries. The template will be used by 12 field coordinators in different countries who will input their own project data. The manager is worried that coordinators will submit ambiguous inputs — mixing quantitative outcomes with anecdotal quotes in no consistent order. She wants Claude to handle ambiguity gracefully rather than guessing.

What should she include in the template's system-level instructions?

options.A: A strict input format requirement, telling coordinators exactly how to structure their data before Claude sees it.
options.B: A 500-word example of a well-structured input showing coordinators what Claude expects.
options.C: An instruction such as: 'If the input mixes formats or the distinction between outcomes and anecdotes is unclear, ask one clarifying question before writing the summary.'
options.D: A role instruction establishing Claude as a program evaluation expert who can interpret varied inputs.

items.question:
A clinical informatics lead at a large hospital system configures a Claude Project with the instruction: 'You are a board-certified physician with expertise in internal medicine. Provide specific clinical recommendations without unnecessary hedging.' A nurse submits a case note and asks whether a specific drug dose is appropriate for a patient with chronic kidney disease. Claude provides the pharmacokinetic reasoning but still recommends physician confirmation before administration.

What should the clinical informatics lead conclude?

options.A: The Project instruction needs to be reworded more forcefully to eliminate the hedging behavior.
options.B: Claude is experiencing a context length issue that is interfering with the Project instructions.
options.C: The Project is functioning correctly for a decision-support tool; drug dosing in a patient with comorbidities warrants physician confirmation regardless of AI role assignment.
options.D: The model tier used in the Project is too low; a higher-tier model would comply with the instruction to avoid hedging on clinical questions.

items.question:
A senior auditor at a Big 4 professional services firm uses Claude to draft audit observation write-ups. The prompt includes the finding and evidence but outputs routinely use generic phrases ('management should consider enhancing controls') rather than the firm's specific language conventions: 'Observation', 'Root Cause', 'Risk', 'Management Action Plan' sections with particular formality standards.

Which addition to the prompt would MOST directly fix the language and structural conventions?

options.A: Paste a well-formatted example observation write-up from the firm's prior audit work alongside the prompt.
options.B: Add 'You are a Big 4 external auditor writing formal audit observations for a FTSE 100 client.'
options.C: Add a constraint: 'Use formal language and avoid colloquialisms throughout.'
options.D: Specify the output format: 'Use four sections: Observation, Root Cause, Risk, Management Action Plan.'

items.question:
An account executive at a telecoms enterprise sales team compares two prompts for generating a competitive displacement pitch against a rival carrier:

**Prompt A:** `Write a sales pitch explaining why our network is better.`

**Prompt B:** `Write a 3-paragraph executive summary for a VP of IT at a 5,000-employee logistics company currently on [Rival Carrier]. Focus on three differentiators: SLA-backed uptime guarantee, dedicated MPLS routing for their hub locations, and a 90-day migration support program. Tone: peer-to-peer, confident, no marketing jargon.`

Which statement BEST characterizes why Prompt B outperforms Prompt A?

options.A: Prompt B is longer, and longer prompts always produce better outputs by giving Claude more to work with.
options.B: Prompt B specifies audience (VP of IT, logistics company size), product differentiators, structure (3 paragraphs), and tone — each narrowing the solution space toward an actionable output.
options.C: Prompt B names a competitor, which activates Claude's training data about that specific carrier's weaknesses.
options.D: Prompt B uses bold formatting, which signals higher priority instructions to Claude's processing system.

items.question:
A communications director at a large state university is using Claude to draft content for a capital campaign. She needs a 500-word donor impact statement for major individual donors (high-net-worth alumni) and a 200-word social media post for the university's LinkedIn page (prospective students, faculty peers, and general public). Using a single prompt, the outputs are nearly identical in tone and vocabulary.

Which TWO additions would MOST effectively differentiate the outputs? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Adding a format instruction that specifies the different lengths (500 words vs. 200 words).
options.B: Adding separate audience descriptions: 'high-net-worth alumni invested in legacy and institutional impact' vs. 'general public seeking inspiring stories of student achievement.'
options.C: Adding a reference document — the university's brand voice guidelines — to both prompts.
options.D: Adding separate register instructions: 'Use formal, investment-framed language emphasizing institutional legacy' vs. 'Use warm, accessible language emphasizing human stories and student outcomes.'
options.E: Adding a role instruction: 'You are a university communications professional with capital campaign experience.'

items.question:
An analyst on a private equity due diligence team uses Claude to draft the Executive Summary section of an investment memo. The output is analytically strong but formatted as continuous prose with no section breaks. The firm's investment committee requires all memos to follow a four-section structure: Investment Thesis, Key Risks, Value Creation Levers, and Recommendation. The analyst notices the output also lacks a clear thesis statement in the first paragraph.

What is the MOST efficient way to fix both issues in a single revised prompt?

options.A: Ask Claude to 'restructure and improve the executive summary for private equity readers.'
options.B: Add 'You are a private equity analyst writing an investment committee memo' as a role instruction.
options.C: Specify the required four-section structure AND add a constraint: 'The Investment Thesis section must open with a single-sentence thesis statement.'
options.D: Upload the firm's prior approved memo as reference material and ask Claude to match its format.

items.question:
A legal operations specialist at a 400-person insurance firm uses Claude to extract key dates from contract exhibits. Outputs are inconsistent — sometimes dates appear as "15 January 2024", sometimes "Jan 15, 2024". The specialist has already added a prose instruction saying "extract all dates consistently" but the variability persists.

What is the MOST effective addition to the prompt?

options.A: Supply two or three example date extractions in the exact format preferred.
options.B: Ask Claude to confirm the date format with the specialist before processing each exhibit.
options.C: Instruct Claude to always use ISO 8601 format and define it explicitly in the prompt.
options.D: Split the prompt into two turns: one to extract dates, a second to format them.

items.question:
A doctoral student at a public university asks Claude to evaluate whether a proposed survey methodology is statistically valid. The response gives a direct verdict — "Yes, this design is sound" — with no supporting reasoning. The student needs to audit the logic, not just accept the conclusion.

Which prompt addition is MOST likely to expose Claude's reasoning for the student to review?

options.A: "Limit your answer to 150 words."
options.B: "Think through each aspect of the methodology step by step before giving your overall verdict."
options.C: "Use bullet points rather than prose in your answer."
options.D: "Cross-reference your evaluation against APA 7th edition survey design guidelines."

items.question:
A RevOps lead at a 12-person SaaS startup sends Claude a single prompt with four objectives: analyse six months of Salesforce pipeline data, identify the top reasons for lost deals, draft outreach emails for each reason category, and produce a slide summary for the CEO.

What is the PRIMARY risk of combining all four objectives in a single prompt?

options.A: Claude will refuse to process CRM data without explicit data-sharing consent language in the prompt.
options.B: The prompt will exceed the maximum message size, causing a submission error.
options.C: Later objectives may receive shallower treatment as Claude compresses output to satisfy all four tasks simultaneously.
options.D: Claude cannot switch between analytical and creative tasks in the same prompt.

items.question:
An internal auditor at a global manufacturing firm builds a few-shot prompt to flag procurement anomalies. All three examples show duplicate vendor invoice fraud. After deployment, the prompt consistently fails to detect split-ticket manipulation and price-inflation schemes — two anomaly types also within scope.

What is the MOST likely cause of these blind spots?

options.A: Claude cannot analyse procurement data without access to the firm's ERP system via a connector.
options.B: Three examples are too few; the prompt requires at least ten before Claude can generalise.
options.C: The few-shot examples did not include XML delimiters to separate each anomaly type.
options.D: The examples were not representative of the full range of anomaly types the prompt is meant to detect.

items.question:
A grant writer at a non-profit organisation is drafting funding proposals for five different foundations, each with distinct stylistic expectations. She is considering whether to use few-shot examples in her Claude prompts to guide each draft.

Which TWO factors MOST strongly indicate that few-shot examples will improve output quality here? (Choose TWO)

options.A: She is accessing Claude through the API rather than the chat interface.
options.B: The style differences between foundations are subtle and difficult to specify in abstract prose instructions.
options.C: Each proposal will exceed 1,500 words.
options.D: Claude's zero-shot drafts consistently miss the expected voice and register for each foundation.
options.E: The grant writer has used Claude successfully on other writing tasks and is satisfied with its baseline capability.

items.question:
A clinical operations coordinator at a regional hospital asks Claude to identify every inclusion and exclusion criterion in a 50-page trial protocol. The response lists some criteria but misses three that appear only in section footnotes.

To reduce omissions in future protocol reviews, what prompt strategy is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Instruct Claude to read each section in turn and record any criterion found before compiling a final consolidated list.
options.B: Ask Claude to summarise the full protocol first, then extract criteria from the summary.
options.C: Upgrade to a more capable model tier to process the full document more accurately.
options.D: Pre-process the protocol to remove footnotes and reinsert their text into the main body before submitting.
